records.issue_text: Controller specs invoke actions directly and bypass route parameter recognition, so they don't catch the :group_id vs :id routing mismatch
records.rationale: The alleged :group_id vs :id mismatch is contradicted by the diff itself: routes.rb adds `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` nested inside `resources :groups`, which produces a :group_id param; the controller uses `params.require(:group_id)` and the specs pass `group_id: group.id` — all consistent. No mismatch exists in the shown code, so the premise of the finding is false.
records.stripped_text: Controller specs invoke actions directly and bypass route parameter recognition, so they don't catch the :group_id vs :id routing mismatch

records.issue_text: New pagination behavior in groups_controller.rb#members (limit/offset defaults, meta.total/limit/offset payload shape) has no spec coverage
records.rationale: The diff rewrites groups_controller#members with nontrivial new pagination behavior (limit default 50, offset handling, meta.total/limit/offset JSON payload) but the only spec changes are for Admin::GroupsController; no spec covers the public members endpoint's new pagination contract, so a regression in total/limit/offset semantics would go unnoticed. This is a specific, substantive test-coverage gap grounded in the diff.

records.issue_text: remove_member deletes the group membership immediately via group.users.delete(user_id) but then reports success/failure based on an unrelated group.save call, causing inconsistent client/server state if save fails after the deletion already succeeded
records.rationale: The diff adds `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)` in remove_member. The membership deletion is committed immediately via users.delete, so the subsequent save's success/failure governs the HTTP response for an operation that already took effect. If save fails for an unrelated reason, the client receives an error while the member was actually removed — a real state/response inconsistency introduced by this diff, analogous to the older code path where deletions were transactional with the response.
records.stripped_text: remove_member deletes the group membership immediately via group.users.delete(user_id) but then reports success/failure based on an unrelated group.save call, causing inconsistent client/server state if save fails after the deletion already succeeded

records.issue_text: usernames input field is not cleared after successfully adding members, causing stale usernames to be resent on subsequent submissions
records.rationale: The addMembers action in admin-group.js.es6 explicitly has the comment '// TODO: should clear the input' and calls model.addMembers(this.get("usernames")) without ever setting usernames to null/empty, so stale usernames persist after submission. Real, verifiable defect introduced by the diff, though acknowledged as a TODO (minor severity).
records.stripped_text: usernames input field is not cleared after successfully adding members, causing stale usernames to be resent on subsequent submissions
